body: Jain, Khizer & Thirumalai studied 8,273 quarterly earnings-call transcripts from 559 S&P BSE 500 firms (2004-2019), measuring tone as optimistic minus pessimistic words. Optimistic tone produced positive short-window abnormal returns but did NOT predict better future operating performance. Retail investors reacted most, which the authors read as investors being misled. The paper is posted as an NSE white paper. Implication for our edge: in India, management cheerfulness is priced but uninformative, so scoring tone alone gives no edge and may push you the wrong way. The edge is checking stated promises against later delivery (the promise tracker). A 'tone minus credibility' gap is a candidate signal: high optimism with a poor delivery record should be overpriced, and understated managements with high delivery should be underpriced. This is a hypothesis to test on our own data. The sample is large caps; small-cap managements may be even more promotional.
title: India: optimistic concall tone moves prices but does not predict operating performance

body: Adjust before comparing an Indian company with a US peer: (1) Leases - Ind AS 116 single model lifts EBITDA and CFO; deduct total lease payments. (2) Interest paid - Ind AS 7 operating or financing; US operating; move it into CFO. (3) Development costs - capitalised under Ind AS 38, expensed under ASC 730; compare on cash R&D. (4) PP&E revaluation - allowed Ind AS 16, prohibited US; revaluation reserves inflate book, depress ROE. (5) Impairment reversals - allowed for non-goodwill under Ind AS 36, prohibited US; watch reversals in other income. (6) LIFO - prohibited Ind AS, allowed US; add LIFO reserve. (7) Provisions - Ind AS 37 >50% probable vs ASC 450 higher bar/low end of range. (8) 'Exceptional items' line common in India (Schedule III); US has no extraordinary items (ASU 2015-01). (9) Bank overdrafts can be cash under Ind AS 7. (10) Componentisation required under Ind AS. (11) Non-GAAP: US Reg G/Item 10(e) reconciliation; India no equivalent - rebuild 'adjusted EBITDA'. (12) Consolidation: control model vs US voting + VIE model. Revenue (Ind AS 115 vs ASC 606) and goodwill (impairment-only) are broadly converged. Upcoming: IFRS 18 (2027) not yet notified in India.
title: Ind AS vs US GAAP differences that change cross-border comparisons (adjustment table)

body: Michaely, Thaler and Womack, 'Price Reactions to Dividend Initiations and Omissions: Overreaction or Drift?' (Journal of Finance 50(2), 1995; ~720 Crossref citations), US NYSE/AMEX 1964-1988: firms initiating a dividend gained about +3.4% in the 3-day window, and firms omitting one lost about -7.0%. Reactions to omissions are roughly twice as large. After the event, prices kept drifting in the same direction: about +7.5% in the year after initiations and about -11% after omissions (longer-horizon drift continued for omitters). The market underreacts to these management signals, consistent with PEAD. Replicated: the announcement asymmetry is robust; the drift has been confirmed in some later samples and weakened in others (Boehme-Sorescu 2002 find the initiation drift weaker with better methods). Use for us: in India, the first dividend of a turnaround company, a promoter-led shift to a payout policy, or a dividend cut or skip by a habitual payer are event signals to log. A first dividend after years of losses is a credible 'cash is real' signal because it costs money to fake. A skipped dividend at a high-pledge promoter group is a liquidity warning (links to group contagion).
title: Dividend initiations +3.4% and omissions -7%, with drift in the same direction for a year (Michaely-Thaler-Womack 1995)
